extracted.intended_audience: federal agency procurement officials, agency heads, and interested parties (e.g., contractors, commentators)
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and publishing a Federal Register transmittal/rescission notice (here, proposed rescission of OMB Circular A-49) including required rationale, cross-references, and instructions for public comment. Also contains NRC procedural requirements for petitions to intervene referenced in the same Federal Register pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period and receipt deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comments you have should be received by this Office on or before December 31, 1985. Comments must be received 60 days from the date of this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transmittal memoranda should establish the requisite comment period before final publication; specify calendar deadline(s) (e.g., specific date and/or number of days from publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should include reference to this notice and be sent to: Mr. Robert C. Bienvenue, Office of Federal Procurement Policy, Room 9013, 726 Jackson Place, NW, Washington, DC 20503.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a named contact, full mailing address (and telephone where appropriate), and require that comments reference the notice; designate an office/room for receipt. If necessary, include alternative submission details (e.g., telephone or other notification instructions for late filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: Our action to rescind the Circular is based on the recommendation of the Assistant Secretaries for Management Group (Reform 88 Program) and our assessment of the adequacy of other existing policies and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the factual and procedural basis for rescission (e.g., recommendations from relevant groups and assessment that other policies/regulations provide adequate coverage). Explain why the existing circular is no longer necessary or is redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of subject matter and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular No. A-49 established general criteria to assist Executive agencies in developing policies for the use of management and operating contracts. Management and operating contracts are used to administer research and development establishments; to administer and operate Government-owned or leased industrial facilities; or to operate such personal or professional services as are authorized by law. This category of contracts has limited applicability in the Executive agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise definition of the instrument or policy being rescinded and clarify its scope and typical uses, including limitations and contexts (e.g., R&D centers, government-owned facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references to current authorities and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy in the Circular is restated in the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 17A. Additionally, where management and operating contracts are used as the funding vehicle for Federal Contract Research Centers, Federally-Funded Research and Development Centers, and/or Federal Laboratories, new policies have been issued to provide guidance in these unique situations, i.e., OFPP Policy Letter 64-1, 'Federally Funded Research and Development Centers,' dated April 4, 1984.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify where policy and guidance governing the subject now reside (FAR, policy letters, directives), citing specific subparts, policy letters, or directives so readers know the controlling documents post-rescission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressee and distribution of transmittal memorandum
rubrics_metrics.description: MEMORANDUM TO HEADS OF DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES ... cc: Procurement Executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the transmittal to the appropriate senior officials and indicate copies/cc to stakeholder groups (e.g., procurement executives) so the rescission reaches responsible officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice drafting requirement: state intended administrative effect
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice provides interested parties with a proposed transmittal memorandum which would rescind OMB Circular No. A-49, 'Use of Management and Operating Contracts' and establishes the requisite comment period before final publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly what the notice does (proposes rescission), and any administrative consequences (e.g., where policy will be found instead). Make explicit whether the action is proposed or final and whether it establishes procedures (such as comment periods) prior to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for leave to intervene — specificity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by 10 CFR 2.714, a petition for leave to intervene shall set forth with particularity the interest of the petitioner in the proceeding, and how that interest may be affected by the results of the proceeding. The petition should specifically explain the reasons why intervention should be permitted with particular reference to the following factors: (1) The nature of the petitioner’s right under the Act to be made a party to the proceeding; (2) the nature and extent of the petitioner’s property, financial or other interest in the proceeding; and (3) the possible effect of any order which may be entered in the proceeding on the petitioner’s interest. The petition should also identify the specific aspect(s) of the subject matter of the proceeding as to which petitioner wishes to intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NRC licensing proceedings, petitions must satisfy detailed specificity requirements addressing legal rights, concrete interests, and potential effects of orders, and must identify precise issues the petitioner seeks to litigate. Failure to meet these specificity requirements can result in denial of intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and supplement deadlines for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has filed a petition for leave to intervene or who has been admitted as a party may amend the petition without requesting leave of the Board up to fifteen (15) days prior to the first prehearing conference scheduled in the proceeding... Not later than fifteen (15) days prior to the first prehearing conference scheduled in the proceeding, a petitioner shall file a supplement to the petition to intervene which must include a list of the contentions which are sought to be litigated in the matter, and the bases for each contention set forth with reasonable specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and publish firm deadlines for amendments and supplements; require that supplements include a list of contentions and bases with reasonable specificity. Warn that failure to file a supplement satisfying requirements with respect to at least one contention will bar participation as a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and notification procedures for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a hearing or a petition for leave to intervene shall be filed with the Secretary of the Commission... or may be delivered to the Commission's Public Document Room... Where petitions are filed during the last ten (10) days of the notice period, it is requested that the petitioner or representative for the petitioner promptly so inform the Commission by a toll-free telephone call to Western Union at (800) 325-6000.... The Western Union operator should be given Datagram Identification Number 3737 and the following message addressed to: [name; petitioner’s contact info; date petition mailed; plant name; publication date and page number of this Federal Register notice]. A copy of the petition should also be sent to the Executive Legal Director... and to counsel for the licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify exact filing locations (Secretary, Public Document Room), and provide special expedited notification procedures for late filings (Western Union/datagram content). Require service copies to designated officials and counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on contentions and consequences of failure to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions shall be limited to matters within the scope of the amendment under construction. A petitioner who fails to file such a supplement which satisfies these requirements with respect to at least one contention will not be permitted to participate as a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the permissible scope of contentions (must be within scope of the amendment) and state the sanction for noncompliance (exclusion from participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for accepting nontimely filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nontimely filings of petitions for leave to intervene, amended petitions, supplemental petitions and/or requests for hearing will not be entertained absent a determination by the Commission, the presiding officer or the presiding Atomic Safety and Licensing Board, that the petition and/or request should be granted based upon a balancing of factors specified in 10 CFR 2.714(a)(1)(i)-(iv) and 2.714(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the regulatory standard and balancing test that governs whether late filings may be accepted, and cite the governing regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and opportunities of permitted intervenors
rubrics_metrics.description: Those permitted to intervene become parties to the proceeding, subject to any limitations in the order granting leave to intervene, and have the opportunity to participate fully in the conduct of the hearing, including the opportunity to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing intervention consequences, spell out procedural rights (presentation of evidence, cross-examination) and the potential for limits imposed by the admitting order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative publication and citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice appears in the Federal Register and includes agency name, action, summary, 'for further information contact' details, supplementary information, and signature block with date. (E.g., 'OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET — Office of Federal Procurement Policy — Proposed Transmittal Memorandum No. 1, Rescission of OMB Circular No. A-49, 'Use of Management and Operating Contracts'').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard Federal Register notice structure: agency caption, action line, summary (human summary), contact info, supplementary information (background, reasoning), dates, addresses for comments, and signature block with official name and title.
